title: Cross-functional accountable map and signal matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet is a compact cross-functional accountability map paired with a signal matrix designed to help product-ops run safe, observable rollouts for roadmap milestones (feature toggles, model swaps, Dedicated capacity launches, and private deployment enablement). Use this during the 2-week launch window and the first 30 days post-launch as the single source for who watches which signal, thresholds for action, and step-by-step escalation.

Snapshot (example release): v2.3 inference-route + default-quantization flip; traffic ramp plan: canary 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 5 days.

Topline owners (cascade):
- Product (release lead): Avery Chen — overall go/no-go, stakeholder comms, adoption targets.
- Eng / Serving runtime: Samir Patel — performance, latency regressions, kernel fallbacks.
- Infra / SRE: Leah O'Connor — capacity, autoscale, region failover.
- Applied ML / Model Ops: Priya Nair — quality regressions, embeddings drift, rollout of model variant.
- Customer Success: Diego Morales — customer impact triage, support doc updates.

Signal matrix (primary signals, owner, threshold, action):
1) Latency p95 (global) — owner: Samir Patel — baseline 220ms; yellow if > 1.3x baseline (286ms) sustained 5m; red if > 2x baseline (440ms) sustained 2m. Actions: yellow -> pause next ramp step, increase batch window; red -> immediate canary rollback and route to fallback model variant.

2) Error rate (5xx / generation failures) — owner: Leah O'Connor — baseline <0.3%; yellow if 0.3–1.0% sustained 10m; red if >1.0% 5m. Actions: yellow -> open incident, switch to lower-capacity pool; red -> cut traffic to hosted fallback + page oncall.

3) Quality signal: hallucination rate on eval set (automated), user escalations / CS tickets — owner: Priya Nair & Diego Morales — threshold: automated regression >5% relative lift vs baseline OR >3 customer severity=high tickets in 24h. Actions: freeze rollout, revert model, start labeled-eval postmortem.

4) Cost per 1M tokens (hosted) — owner: Product Ops (Avery) & Finance — threshold: +30% vs target. Actions: evaluate batching/quantization, pause non-essential traffic, hold billing review.

5) Adoption / success metrics (feature-specific) — owner: Product — metric examples: CTR, completions per session, retention lift. Yellow if metric movement diverges by confidence interval; red if primary adoption KPI regresses >10% absolute. Actions: halt feature ramp, revert flags for user cohort.

Gates & checklist (pre-ramp):
- [ ] Canary playbook validated in staging + dry run (SRE lead).
- [ ] Observability feeds active in Redwood Console: per-route P95, P99, cost breakdown, trace links.
- [ ] Alerts configured (Slack + pager) for latency p95, error rate, and quality regression.
- [ ] Rollback procedure documented with runbook links and test rollback executed.
- [ ] Customer comms draft prepared for top 10 enterprise accounts.
- [ ] Support KB + runbook updated for CS.

Ramp plan template (uses canary cohorts):
- Day 0: canary 2% (internal + 5 pilot customers) — 4h stabilize window
- Day 1: ramp to 10% if no yellow/red signals for 12h
- Day 2–3: ramp to 50% with continuous monitoring and staggered region enablement
- Day 4: full 100% if stable for 48h

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Any red signal as defined in the Signal matrix -> immediate rollback to previous model or route variant.
- Two independent yellow signals persisting >30 minutes -> pause and investigate; severity check to decide rollback.

Contingencies and mitigations:
- Fallback models: maintain a compatible quantized variant that can serve at lower cost and lower latency.
- Traffic re-routing: have policy to route enterprise traffic to Dedicated pools to preserve SLA.
- Capacity shortage: SRE to burst to reserved nodes or spin up region fallback.

KPI definitions (canonical):
- Latency_p95_ms: measured at Redwood edge per-route, exclude retries.
- Error_rate_pct: 5xx / total requests (generation failures + infra errors).
- Cost_per_1M_tokens_usd: total infra + model-licensing costs allocated to route divided by tokens served * 1M.
- Quality_regression_pct: automated eval delta on holdout prompt-set (normalized).
- Adoption_delta_pct: relative change vs baseline cohort over 7d.

Dashboard columns to populate in daily morning check (template):
Date | Route | Canary % | Latency_p95 | Error_rate | Cost_1M_tokens | Quality_delta | Adoption_delta | Owner | Status | Notes

Escalation path (phone/Slack/pager):
- Primary oncall (SRE): Leah O'Connor — escalate to Eng Platform lead -> Samir Patel -> Product (Avery) -> CTO if cross-customer impact.

After-action cadence (post-rollback or full ramp):
- T+1 day: 30-minute sync with owners to capture immediate causes.
- T+3 days: 90-minute cross-functional RCA and remediation plan with owners and timeline.
- T+14 days: Validation window to confirm fixes and re-run targeted evals.

Open questions & to-do (living):
- Are route-level cost attributions accurate for private deployments? (Action: Finance + Infra to confirm by EOD +7)
- Need an automated signal that links Console trace IDs to customer ticket IDs for faster triage. (Action: DevEx + Observability)
- Should default canary size be 1% for low-risk infra fixes? (Decision needed from Product council)

Next steps before the next release review:
- Product Ops to finalize canary cohort list and confirm pilot customer consent.
- SRE to run a stress test hitting p99 scenarios in staging and publish results to linked_confluence_page.
- Applied ML to validate model variant on new quantization profile and provide sample outputs for CS.

Notes to reviewers: This is intentionally compact and prescriptive — the goal is to cut decision latency during rollouts. Please annotate the signal thresholds you disagree with and add alternate mitigations inline (use comments).

Change log (brief):
- 2024-10-22: initial draft created (Avery).
- 2024-10-29: added cost thresholds and adoption columns (Finance feedback).
- 2024-11-05: updated escalation path and owners (in review).
